top_categories.workout_context: 13,264ft of climbing means repeated surges above threshold. VO2max work is how you survive the fifth climb, not just the first.
145ft/mi means long efforts at or near FTP on every climb. If your threshold cracks at minute 15, you'll walk the rest.
At mile 60 of 91, glycogen is gone. This workout teaches your body to produce watts on fumes.
At GFNY Grand Ballon, surges push you above threshold and you have to recover while still riding. Over-unders train exactly that.
Race-pace efforts that mimic GFNY Grand Ballon's demands. Pacing, fueling, and tactical decisions under fatigue. Practice the race before July.
Every hard session works better with a bigger aerobic base. At 91 miles, base fitness is the difference between racing and surviving.
13,264ft of climbing on grades that change every minute. You need to switch from seated to standing without losing rhythm.
88–92% FTP is where you'll spend the hardest sustained miles of GFNY Grand Ballon. Train it until it feels boring.
GFNY Grand Ballon's mixed terrain forces constant power changes. Accelerate over rises and out of corners, settle on the open road, and repeat for 91 miles.
Low-cadence force work for 13,264ft of climbing. The slow, grinding ascents where you can't spin—you push.
How long can you hold 105% FTP before you blow? At GFNY Grand Ballon, that number decides whether you bridge or get dropped.
The aerobic base that lets you ride mixed terrain at tempo for 91 miles without cracking. No shortcuts.

race_overlay.heat: July in Thann, Alsace, France can bring heat. Complete 3–4 heat exposure sessions in the final 2 weeks before GFNY Grand Ballon. Increase sodium intake 48 hours before race day.
race_overlay.nutrition: Target 60–80g carbs/hour for GFNY Grand Ballon’s 91 miles. Start fueling within the first 30 minutes — early fueling prevents late-race collapse. Bonking at mile 60 is a nutrition failure, not a fitness failure.
race_overlay.altitude: GFNY Grand Ballon with 13,264ft of climbing, much of it above 8,000ft demands altitude preparation. Arrive 5–7 days early for acclimatization. Expect 5–15% power reduction at altitude. Increase iron intake 4 weeks out. Hydrate aggressively — altitude increases fluid loss by 20–40%.
race_overlay.terrain: Mixed terrain at GFNY Grand Ballon requires surface adaptability. Include weekly rides on mixed terrain to build confidence.

pack_summary: This 10-workout pack focuses on VO2max, TT Threshold, and Durability to prepare you for 91 miles of mixed terrain in Thann, Alsace, France.
